WEEK 04 · FOUNDATIONS
BEST FOR FIRST-TIMERS

KIT NO. PP-W04-WS

Walnut Wall Shelf

A single-board floating shelf in oiled black walnut. You'll learn how to mill a square edge, drill perpendicular holes, and finish a surface that earns compliments. Hangs three pots, two books, or one well-loved cup.

PRICE
$64.00
or 3× $21.33 — no interest

across one calm afternoon

BUILD TIMELINE · 6 STEPS · 2H 30M
How you'll build it
Watch the 4-minute walkthrough
1
15 min

Lay out the keyhole positions from the printed template.

LAYOUT
2
25 min

Drill pilot holes square to the back face of the board.

DRILLING
3
20 min

Recess and seat the brass keyhole plates flush.

FITTING
4
35 min

Sand through 120 → 180 → 320, always with the grain.

SURFACING
5
30 min

Apply the hard-wax oil, wipe back, then buff to a soft sheen.

FINISHING
6
25 min

Locate studs (or set anchors) and hang the shelf level.

MOUNTING
Hover the ? on any step for a 30-second clip of the technique it teaches.

Marisol P.
FIRST PROJECT EVER
Week 04 of path
·
Feb 18, 2024
"I actually used a drill for the first time."

The keyhole template made me brave. I was sure I'd split the walnut, and instead I drilled four perfect holes and texted my mom. Finish is silky after two coats. Already eyeing Week 05.

Verified build · finished in 2h 10m
Devon Halloway
WEEK 09 OF PATH
·
Feb 06, 2024
"A clean little win between bigger builds."

I came back to this from Week 09 to make one for my partner's plants. Took about ninety minutes. The hard-wax oil is genuinely lovely — better than the brand I'd been buying separately.

Verified build · second time builder

"The plan booklet reads like a friend talking."

No jargon, real photos for the tricky bits, and a checklist I could tape to the wall. I made one mistake (sanded across the grain on coat one) and the printed troubleshooting page told me exactly how to fix it.

Verified build · finished in 2h 45m
Toby K.
WEEK 14 OF PATH
·
Jan 12, 2024
"Gave one as a housewarming gift."

Ordered two — one to keep, one wrapped in butcher paper with the unused sandpaper as a joke. Both look like they came from a tiny shop in Brooklyn. The walnut grain on mine had a beautiful curl near one end.
